crime: Each night at lockup, {WITCH_NAME} carried one cup of warm milk down the cell corridor, and from that single cup she passed a copy through every barred cell door.
For weeks, one girl kept her company at the upper railing each dusk, yet turned down every copy she was offered, even of the sleeping drug she took each night. "One is enough," the girl said.
One dusk, after the others had gone in, the girl put her nightly pill in {WITCH_NAME}'s palm. "I slept without it. I won't need it anymore."
Once, when {WITCH_NAME} was small, her mother had put her own nightly pill back into that palm. "I don't need it anymore." By morning she was gone.

There at the railing, the one pill in her hand became a handful, every one alike. At lockup she dropped the handful into the last cup and passed it through the girl's barred door, as she did every night.

At unlock, the prisoners found the girl still in her bunk bed, with two pills left whole at the bottom of her cup. In the trial court they ruled that she had swallowed pills she had saved up herself. She had refused every copy; {WITCH_NAME} had never once held her pill.

Then one prisoner noticed that the two pills from her cup had the same chipped corner. The prisoners understood: pills alike down to the chip were {WITCH_NAME}'s copies. She had held the girl's pill after all.
fields.epitaph: She never could give anyone just one.
fields.epithet: The Hand That Must Be Needed
execution: The execution stand raises a giant iron cup. She sits chained at its bottom. An iron hand tips an iron pitcher over the rim, and milk pours in, on and on, never running dry. It climbs over her chest, then her chin; she strains up against the chain as the milk closes over her mouth. Then the milk lies still to the brim, and nothing rises through it.

magic.name: Enough to Go Around
magic.text: She turns any lifeless thing in her hands into several identical, real copies.
